evidence: Catull. 4.25–26: sed haec prius fuēre: nunc …
Liv. 21.54.2: nunc corpora cūrāre tempus est
terms.comment: The present as against before or after: prius … nunc, nunc … ōlim.

terms.gloss: now (by now, at last); in a moment
evidence: Traupman 88: now, nunc; (denoting emphasis and urgency) jam
terms.comment: Jam marks a point reached: what is so now and was not before (jam advesperāscit, it’s getting dark now), or, with a future, what is about to happen (see in a moment).

terms.gloss: for now, at the moment, for the time being
evidence: Cic. Att. 15.20.4: hoc videō in praesentiā opus esse (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: sed haec prius fuēre: nunc recondita senet quiēte
phrases.english: but all that was before: now it is laid up and grows old in peace
now is the time to look after ourselves

phrases.latin: nōn, sī male nunc, et ōlim sīc erit
phrases.english: if things are bad now, they will not always be so

sources: Lewis & Short: nunc · Lewis & Short: jam · Lewis & Short: praesens · Lewis & Short: posthac
